newsitem.title: USA: Oldest U.S. working nuclear plant faces closure or sale.
newsitem.headline: Oldest U.S. working nuclear plant faces closure or sale.

text.p: The nation's oldest operating nuclear power plant may be too expensive to operate in this era of deregulated power, its owner said Thursday.

Parsippany, N.J.-based GPU Inc. said it is studying the sale or early retirement of the Oyster Creek Nuclear Generating Station, which is now licensed to operate until 2009. The plant is located in Lacy Township on New Jersey's south Atlantic coast.
The company can buy power on the open market cheaper than it costs to produce it at the Oyster Creek plant, GPU Energy President Dennis Baldassari said.

A sale or shutdown at this time would reduce GPU's costs by 3.7 cents per kilowatt hour for the power the plant produces, he said. The company could purchase electricity on the open market at current spot prices of 2 cents to 2.5 cents per kilowatt hour, he added.
The plant's age, by itself, is not one of the factors resulting in the decision to look at sale or early retirement, GPU Nuclear Inc. Chief Executive T. Gary Broughton said.
The plant went into commercial operation in December 1969. It was built by General Electric Co. at a cost of just $90 million.

But safety improvements and other upgrades since then have cost the company more than $700 million, President Fred Hafer said. The next oldest plant is Nine Mile Point Unit 1 located on Lake Ontario in northern New York state. It is operated by the Niagara Mohawk Power Corp.

GPU Energy is the trade name for the three operating utility subsidiaries of GPU --Jersey Central Power & Light, Metropolitan Edison and Pennsylvania Electric -- which provide power to nearly 2 million customers in Pennsylvania and New Jersey.
